scenes.text: People say data is the new oil. [1] For AI, it's even more than that, because a model can only be as good as the data it learns from. [2] Let's understand training data.

Training data is the collection of examples a model learns from. [1] It can be text, images, audio or numbers. [2] For LLMs, it's trillions of words from books and the web. [3] For vision models, millions of photos. [4] And for a spam filter, thousands of emails.

data.definition: The collection of examples a model learns from.

scenes.text: Before training, data goes through a pipeline. [1] First, collect, gather lots of examples. [2] Then clean, remove duplicates, junk and errors. [3] Label, add the right answers, often done by humans. [4] Split, keeping some data aside for testing, [5] and only then, train the model.

So what makes data good? [1] Quantity, enough examples to learn from. [2] Quality, correct and clean. [3] Diversity, covering many people, places and situations. [4] And freshness, up to date, so the world hasn't moved on.

There's a famous rule, garbage in, garbage out. [1] If a face recognition model mostly sees light skinned faces, it can fail on darker skin. [2] With diverse, balanced data, it works fairly for everyone.

So why keep some data aside? [1] The training set, which the model learns from. [2] The validation set, used to tune settings during training. [3] And the test set, kept completely hidden, like a final exam the model has never seen.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think more data is always better. [2] More helps, but only if it's good. A smaller, clean, well labelled dataset often beats a huge messy one. Quality usually matters more than quantity.

data.fact: Only good data helps. A clean, well-labelled dataset often beats a huge messy one.

scenes.text: Quick quiz! Why keep a test set hidden from the model during training? [1] Pause and think, and if you get it right, comment below! <pause 3.2> [2] To check how it does on data it has never seen, just like a real exam!

data.question: We hide the test set to…
options: Check it on data it's never seen

scenes.text: Let's recap. [1] Training data is what the model learns from. [2] It's collected, cleaned, labelled and split. [3] Good data is high quality, diverse and fresh.
